subtask1_wikievents_kappa.interpretation: WikiEvents has the tightest schema by far (κ̄=0.029 vs SciERC=0.38, DocRED=0.82). With 27 entity types and highly specific role-type constraints (avg 21.2 valid pairs vs 729 possible), the constraint space is ~97% pruned per event type. This explains why constrained decoding eliminates violations so effectively on WikiEvents.

subtask2_70b_cf.note: 70B experiment is DocRED only (Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-AWQ-INT4). No 70B SciERC experiment exists.
subtask2_70b_cf.cf_counting_discrepancy: analysis_v2 (7.01%) uses fixed_20260514_v2 checker; unified_eval (5.15%) counts 856 CF entities / 16606 total predicted entities; TCR (11.61%) counts 1988 CF entities / 17120 unique entities with a more aggressive entity-level scan
subtask2_70b_cf.interpretation: The 70B CF rate (5-7%) is 2-3x higher than 8B ZS (2.57%) and 20-30x higher than 8B FT (0.2-0.3%). Primary causes: (1) Zero-shot setting — fine-tuning teaches schema compliance, drastically reducing CF; (2) INT4 quantization likely contributes — reduced precision may degrade type consistency for entity mentions appearing in multiple relations; (3) Not a pure scale effect — 8B ZS Llama also shows high CF (1357 entities), suggesting the ZS→FT gap is the dominant factor.

subtask4_r_f1_range.verdict: The ±0.6pp claim holds for R-F1 on RE datasets (SciERC, DocRED): max |Δ|=0.30pp. However, WikiEvents Llama FT shows Arg-F1 delta of −1.07pp (constrained underperforms unconstrained), exceeding the ±0.6pp bound. If the abstract claim is scoped to R-F1 only, it is accurate. If intended to cover all datasets including WikiEvents Arg-F1, it needs qualification — either widen to ±1.1pp or explicitly exclude WikiEvents (where CIs overlap anyway, so the difference is not statistically significant).
